decisions_and_open_items.detail: The supplied image gives total ascent times of 1, 2 and 2 minutes at 10, 20 and 30 feet. S2 p.5 mentions a minimum three-minute total stop time in its shallow example. S2 pp.2 and 4–6 also express the initial ascent rate as 30 versus 33 ft/min. No universal shallow-stop algorithm or emergency deco schedule was invented. The published table matches S14; profile details require the trained procedure.
S12 describes accidental NDL exceedance and explicitly excludes planned use. Article states that distinction; it does not publish a new emergency-deco calculator or extrapolate the examples.

decisions_and_open_items.status: Illustrative model clarified; no formula/default changes
decisions_and_open_items.detail: Existing default 100-foot model produces 8 minutes, about 40.24 cu ft and 1,600 psi in AL80; source rounds the average to 2.5 ATA and gets 40 cu ft. Other depths are calculated examples, not source-issued UTD reserve tables. Model uses maximum depth, rounded first stop and conservative segment approximations; it is not the recreational NDL/ascent planner.

This review aligns the available article copy to the supplied versions: UTD v6c, v4.1 instructor playbooks and 2020 instructional slides. It is not verification that these are the current governing standards or UTD certification/endorsement. GUE curricula, historical claims, local water conditions and owner business facts are not established by these PDFs.
